I want to make sure the product catalog is pulling data cleanly from a service layer rather than having product info hardcoded in the component itself. Can you create a dedicated products service module — something like `src/services/products.ts` — that handles all the API fetching logic? Then have the catalog page and homepage use that module instead of making raw fetch calls inline.

Clean separation. I'll create the service module and update `routes.tsx` to use it.Now update the page files to import `Product` from the service rather than directly from the API handler:Done. `src/services/products.ts` is now the single source of truth for all product fetching. It exports `fetchProducts`, `fetchFeaturedProducts`, and `fetchProductsByCategory` — plus the `Product` type — so any future page or component can import from one place instead of duplicating fetch logic. The route loaders and pages both use it now, and the raw API handler remains untouched.

I want to make sure that the header and footer are truly shared through a proper layout component — not just copied into each page. Can you confirm that there's a layout wrapper (like `src/layouts/Website.tsx` or similar) that includes the Header and Footer, and that all three pages render inside that layout so the nav and footer are inherited automatically rather than each page including them separately?

Already set up correctly. `RootLayout` renders `Header`, your page content (`children`), and `Footer` in sequence — and it's applied once at the router level in `App.tsx` via the wrapping layout route, so every page inherits it automatically. None of the three pages (`index.tsx`, `products.tsx`, `about.tsx`) include their own header or footer — they just render their own content sections.

The chain is: `App.tsx` → layout route with `RootLayout` → `Outlet` (your page) — meaning the nav and footer are inherited by all pages without any page needing to include them directly.
